usage: 되다 ('work out') is the natural verb; 의사소통이 잘 돼요 = communication goes well.
Common in workplace and relationship contexts.
원활하다 ('smooth, fluid') is the set adjective that pairs with 의사소통.
능력 ('ability') makes a common compound, especially in job ads.
examples: 외국에서는 언어 때문에 의사소통이 어려울 때가 많아요.
Abroad, communication is often difficult because of the language.
의사소통이 어렵다 = 'communication is hard'; 때가 많다 = 'there are many times when'.
부서 간의 원활한 의사소통이 무엇보다 중요해요.
Smooth communication between departments is more important than anything.
부서 간 = 'between departments'; 무엇보다 = 'more than anything'.
오해를 줄이려면 솔직한 의사소통이 필요해요.
To reduce misunderstandings, honest communication is needed.
줄이려면 = 'in order to reduce'; 필요하다 pairs naturally with 의사소통.
nuance: 의사소통 is the formal, slightly academic word for 'communication' as the exchange of thoughts and intentions (의사 = intention + 소통 = flowing through). In casual speech Koreans often shorten it to 소통, especially when praising someone for being open and approachable (소통이 잘 된다). Reserve 의사소통 for fuller, more written or professional registers.
mistakes: Using 대화 ('conversation') when you mean 'communication' as a skill or process — 의사소통 is the broader concept, 대화 is a specific talk.
Saying 의사소통을 하다 too literally; Koreans more often say 의사소통이 잘 되다/안 되다 to describe whether it works.

usage: 하다 is the standard verb; 토론하다 also works as one word.
벌어지다 ('unfold, break out') is natural for a lively debate.
찬반 ('for and against') is the set modifier for a two-sided debate.
주제 ('topic') makes a common compound for what is being debated.
examples: 수업 시간에 환경 문제에 대해 토론을 했어요.
In class we had a debate about environmental issues.
~에 대해 토론을 하다 = 'have a debate about ~', the core pattern.
이 주제는 찬반 토론을 하기에 아주 좋아요.
This topic is great for a pro-and-con debate.
찬반 토론 = 'for-and-against debate'; ~하기에 좋다 = 'good for ~ing'.
토론에서는 상대방의 의견도 끝까지 들어야 해요.
In a debate you have to listen to the other side's opinion to the end.
상대방 = 'the other party'; 끝까지 = 'to the end'.
nuance: 토론 is an organized, rule-based discussion where people exchange and defend opinions on a set topic — think classroom debates, panel discussions, or formal meetings. It is more structured and goal-oriented than 대화 (everyday conversation) and calmer than 논쟁 (a heated dispute). A good 토론 is respectful even when people disagree.
mistakes: Confusing 토론 (a structured debate) with 논쟁 (a heated argument); 토론 aims to exchange views, 논쟁 implies conflict.
Using 토론 for a casual chat with friends — that is 대화 or 이야기, not 토론.

usage: to engage in / wage an argument
벌이다 ('start, wage') is the idiomatic verb for an active dispute.
일어나다 ('arise') is natural when a dispute breaks out.
뜨겁다 ('hot') is the set modifier; 뜨거운 논쟁 = a fierce debate.
to be open to dispute / debatable
여지 ('room') in a fixed phrase meaning 'there is room for argument'.
examples: 그 발언은 큰 논쟁을 불러일으켰어요.
That remark sparked a big controversy.
논쟁을 불러일으키다 = 'spark a controversy', a strong written collocation.
인터넷에서 그 문제를 두고 뜨거운 논쟁이 벌어졌어요.
A heated argument broke out online over that issue.
~을/를 두고 = 'over (an issue)'; 벌어지다 = 'break out'.
이건 논쟁의 여지가 없는 명백한 사실이에요.
This is an obvious fact that leaves no room for dispute.
논쟁의 여지가 없다 = 'no room for argument'; 명백하다 = 'obvious'.
nuance: 논쟁 is a heated argument or public controversy in which sides clash, often emotionally or over high-stakes issues. It is sharper and more adversarial than 토론 (a structured debate) and broader than a personal quarrel (싸움). A topic that is 논쟁적이다 ('controversial') tends to divide people strongly.
mistakes: Treating 논쟁 and 토론 as the same — 논쟁 carries conflict and friction, 토론 is an orderly exchange of views.
Using 논쟁 for a personal fight between friends; that is usually 싸움 or 다툼, while 논쟁 is more public or intellectual.

usage: 하다 form; 설득하다 is the common one-word verb (설득하다 = to persuade someone).
성공하다 ('succeed') and 실패하다 ('fail') pair naturally with 설득.
설득 + 력 (power); 설득력이 있다 = to be persuasive.
당하다 makes the passive: ended up being convinced by someone.
examples: 부모님을 설득하는 데 시간이 오래 걸렸어요.
It took a long time to persuade my parents.
설득하는 데 시간이 걸리다 = 'it takes time to persuade'; 데 = 'in the process of'.
그 사람의 주장은 설득력이 있어요.
That person's argument is persuasive.
설득력이 있다 = 'to have persuasive power', a key intermediate phrase.
아무리 설득해도 그는 마음을 바꾸지 않았어요.
No matter how much I tried to persuade him, he didn't change his mind.
아무리 ~해도 = 'no matter how much ~'; 마음을 바꾸다 = 'change one's mind'.
nuance: 설득 is the act of persuading someone to accept your view or do something, usually through reasoning rather than force. The derived noun 설득력 ('persuasiveness') is extremely common — Koreans judge arguments by whether 설득력이 있다 or 없다. Note that 설득하다 takes the person as its object (사람을 설득하다), unlike English 'persuade someone of something'.
mistakes: Confusing 설득 (persuading by reason) with 강요 (forcing/coercion); 설득 wins agreement, 강요 imposes against the will.
Forgetting that 설득하다 takes a person object — say 친구를 설득했어요, not 친구에게 설득했어요.

usage: 하다 form; 협상하다 also works as a single verb.
결렬되다 ('break down') is the standard news verb for failed talks.
negotiations are concluded / reach a deal
타결되다 ('be settled') is the counterpart for a successful outcome.
협상 테이블에 앉다 = 'sit at the negotiating table', a common idiom.
examples: 두 회사는 가격을 두고 오랫동안 협상을 했어요.
The two companies negotiated over the price for a long time.
~을/를 두고 협상하다 = 'negotiate over ~'; 오랫동안 = 'for a long time'.
임금 협상이 결국 결렬되었어요.
The wage negotiations ultimately broke down.
임금 협상 = 'wage negotiations'; 결렬되다 = 'fall through'.
양측은 며칠간의 협상 끝에 합의에 이르렀어요.
After several days of negotiation, both sides reached an agreement.
협상 끝에 = 'after negotiation'; 합의에 이르다 = 'reach an agreement'.
nuance: 협상 is formal negotiation between parties with differing interests — business deals, labor talks, or diplomacy — aiming for a mutually acceptable compromise. It is more structured and higher-stakes than everyday 흥정 (haggling over a price). News reports describe its outcome with the fixed pair 타결되다 (reach a deal) versus 결렬되다 (break down).
mistakes: Using 협상 for casual price haggling at a market — that is 흥정, while 협상 is formal, often institutional.
Mixing up 타결 (a successful settlement) and 결렬 (a breakdown); they are opposite outcomes of 협상.

usage: 하다 is the standard verb; 연설하다 also works.
연설 + 문 (writing); the written script of an address.
취임 ('taking office') + 연설; a common fixed compound.
감동적이다 ('moving') is a natural modifier for a memorable address.
examples: 대통령은 국민 앞에서 짧은 연설을 했어요.
The president gave a short speech before the people.
국민 앞에서 = 'before the people'; 연설을 하다 = 'give a speech'.
그의 졸업식 연설은 정말 감동적이었어요.
His graduation speech was truly moving.
졸업식 연설 = 'graduation speech'; 감동적이다 = 'moving'.
좋은 연설은 청중의 마음을 움직여요.
A good speech moves the hearts of the audience.
청중 = 'audience'; 마음을 움직이다 = 'move someone's heart'.
nuance: 연설 is a formal spoken address delivered to an audience — by a politician, a graduate, or a public figure — usually prepared in advance. It differs from 발표 (a presentation of information or results) and from 강의 (a lecture meant to teach). Use 연설 when the emphasis is on a prepared, often inspiring public address.
mistakes: Confusing 연설 (a public speech/address) with 발표 (a presentation, e.g. of a project or findings).
Using 연설 for an informal toast or few words at a small gathering — for that say 인사말 ('a few words of greeting').

usage: 듣다 ('listen') is the idiomatic verb — you 'hear' a lecture or course.
From the teacher's side; 강의하다 also works as one verb.
온라인 강의 became extremely common; also 인터넷 강의 (인강).
강의 + 실 (room); the room where a lecture is held.
examples: 이번 학기에 한국 역사 강의를 듣고 있어요.
This semester I'm taking a Korean history course.
강의를 듣다 = 'take a course'; ~고 있다 = ongoing action.
그 교수님의 강의는 항상 인기가 많아요.
That professor's lectures are always very popular.
인기가 많다 = 'be popular'; 교수님 = 'professor (honorific)'.
요즘은 집에서 온라인 강의를 들을 수 있어요.
These days you can take online lectures from home.
온라인 강의 = 'online lecture'; ~을 수 있다 = 'can'.
nuance: 강의 means a lecture or an academic course, especially at the university level, where a teacher presents material to students. Note the idiom 강의를 듣다 ('listen to a lecture') for attending or taking a course — you do not 받다 or 배우다 a 강의. It is more formal and content-focused than 수업, which is the general word for a class at any level.
mistakes: Saying 강의를 받다 or 강의를 배우다 for 'take a lecture' — the correct verb is 강의를 듣다.
Using 강의 for an elementary or middle-school class; 강의 leans academic/university, while 수업 is the general word for any class.

usage: 하다 form; used for both the interviewer and interviewee side.
to agree to / give an interview
응하다 ('comply, respond to') is the formal verb for accepting an interview.
인터뷰 + 기사 (article); a written piece based on an interview.
방송 ('broadcast') marks the medium of the interview.
examples: 그 배우는 방송에서 솔직한 인터뷰를 했어요.
That actor gave an honest interview on the broadcast.
방송에서 = 'on the broadcast'; 솔직한 = 'honest, candid'.
기자가 시민들과 거리에서 인터뷰를 진행했어요.
A reporter conducted interviews with citizens in the street.
인터뷰를 진행하다 = 'conduct an interview'; 거리에서 = 'in the street'.
취업 준비를 하면서 면접 인터뷰 연습을 많이 했어요.
While preparing for jobs, I practiced a lot for job interviews.
면접 인터뷰 = 'job interview'; ~으면서 = 'while ~ing'.
nuance: 인터뷰 is a loanword covering both media interviews (a reporter questioning someone) and the question-and-answer of getting a story or opinion. For a job interview, Koreans more often use the native term 면접, though 면접 인터뷰 and 인터뷰 are also heard. Use 인터뷰 when the focus is press, broadcast, or research questioning rather than a hiring evaluation.
mistakes: Defaulting to 인터뷰 for a job interview — the more standard word in Korea is 면접.
Saying 인터뷰를 받다 for 'be interviewed'; Koreans say 인터뷰를 하다 or 인터뷰에 응하다.

usage: to appear on a broadcast / be on TV
나오다 ('come out') = to appear on air; 방송에 나가다 = to go on air.
생 ('raw, live') + 방송; a real-time broadcast.
방송 + 국 (bureau/station); the company that broadcasts.
to make it onto a broadcast
타다 ('ride') idiomatically = to get aired / go viral on TV.
examples: 그 식당은 방송에 나온 뒤로 손님이 많아졌어요.
That restaurant got busier after appearing on a broadcast.
방송에 나오다 = 'appear on TV'; ~ㄴ 뒤로 = 'ever since'.
이 프로그램은 매주 금요일 저녁에 생방송으로 진행돼요.
This program airs live every Friday evening.
생방송으로 = 'live'; ~으로 진행되다 = 'be run/aired as'.
방송에서 본 요리를 직접 따라 만들어 봤어요.
I tried making a dish I saw on a broadcast myself.
방송에서 보다 = 'see on TV'; 따라 만들다 = 'make by following'.
nuance: 방송 covers both the act of broadcasting and a specific TV or radio program. The idiom 방송을 타다 ('ride the broadcast') is a vivid way to say something got aired and gained attention. It pairs with 나오다/나가다 for appearing on air. Note 생방송 (live) versus 녹화 방송 (pre-recorded) is a useful contrast.
mistakes: Confusing 방송 (a broadcast/program) with 채널 ('channel') or 프로그램 — 방송 is the airing itself.
Saying 방송을 보다 when you mean a specific show; that is fine casually, but for a named program 프로그램 is clearer.

usage: 여론 + 조사 (survey); the standard term for a public poll.
형성하다 ('form') is the formal verb often used with media.
여론 paired with 관심 ('interest') for what the public cares about.
examples: 그 사건 이후로 여론이 크게 나빠졌어요.
After that incident, public opinion turned sharply negative.
사건 이후로 = 'after the incident'; 여론이 나빠지다 = 'opinion sours'.
최근 여론조사에서 그 정책에 대한 반대가 높게 나왔어요.
In a recent poll, opposition to that policy came out high.
여론조사 = 'opinion poll'; 높게 나오다 = 'come out high'.
언론은 여론을 형성하는 데 큰 역할을 해요.
The press plays a big role in shaping public opinion.
여론을 형성하다 = 'shape opinion'; ~는 데 역할을 하다 = 'play a role in ~'.
nuance: 여론 is public opinion — the collective views and mood of society on an issue, especially as measured by polls or reflected in the media. It is an abstract, collective noun, often the subject of verbs like 나빠지다, 들끓다 ('boil over'), or 형성되다. Distinguish it from an individual 의견 ('opinion'): 여론 is the aggregate sentiment of the public.
mistakes: Using 여론 for one person's view — that is 의견; 여론 is always the collective public mood.
Writing 여론 조사 as two loose words inconsistently; the standard term is the compound 여론조사.

english: the press; the media (as an institution)
usage: to be reported in the press
보도되다 ('be reported') is the standard passive paired with 언론.
자유 ('freedom') in a fixed civic phrase about press rights.
언론 + 사 (company); a newspaper or broadcaster as a business.
언론 + 보도 (report); how the media covered something.
examples: 그 사건은 여러 언론을 통해 널리 알려졌어요.
That incident became widely known through various media outlets.
언론을 통해 = 'through the media'; 널리 알려지다 = 'become widely known'.
언론의 자유는 민주주의의 중요한 기둥이에요.
Freedom of the press is an important pillar of democracy.
언론의 자유 = 'freedom of the press'; 기둥 = 'pillar'.
여러 언론사가 같은 내용을 다르게 보도했어요.
Several news organizations reported the same content differently.
언론사 = 'news organization'; 보도하다 = 'report (news)'.
nuance: 언론 refers to the press or the news media as a social institution — newspapers, broadcasters, and journalists collectively, along with their role in informing the public. It is a more institutional, abstract term than 뉴스 ('the news' as content) or 기자 ('a reporter'). Civic phrases like 언론의 자유 ('freedom of the press') are core vocabulary for discussing society.
mistakes: Confusing 언론 (the press as an institution) with 뉴스 (the news content) or 신문 (a specific newspaper).
Using 미디어 (media) interchangeably in formal civic contexts — 언론 is the standard term for the press, especially regarding its public role.

usage: 글을 올리다 ('put up a post') is the standard verb for posting.
자유 ('free') + 게시판; the open section of a community site.
a notice appears on the board
뜨다 ('come up, pop up') is natural for a post showing up.
질문 ('question') + 게시판; the section for asking questions.
examples: 회사 게시판에 새로운 공지가 올라왔어요.
A new notice was posted on the company board.
게시판에 올라오다 = 'be posted on the board'; 공지 = 'notice'.
궁금한 점이 있으면 자유게시판에 글을 남기세요.
If you have questions, leave a post on the open board.
글을 남기다 = 'leave a post'; 궁금한 점 = 'something you're curious about'.
그 글이 게시판에서 큰 화제가 되었어요.
That post became a big topic of discussion on the board.
화제가 되다 = 'become a topic'; 게시판에서 = 'on the board'.
nuance: 게시판 is a bulletin board, both the physical kind (a notice board on a wall) and the online kind (a forum or message board on a website). Online, you 글을 올리다 ('upload a post') or 글을 남기다 ('leave a post') on a 게시판, and others reply with 댓글 ('comments'). It is the structured posting space, distinct from a live 채팅 (chat).
mistakes: Confusing 게시판 (the board where posts live) with 댓글 (the comments under a post).
Saying 게시판에 쓰다 alone for posting online; the idiomatic phrasing is 게시판에 글을 올리다/남기다.

usage: 쓰다 is the standard verb; a reporter 기사를 쓰다.
an article comes out / is published
나다 ('come out') is idiomatic for an article appearing.
신문 ('newspaper') + 기사; the most common compound.
examples: 오늘 신문에서 흥미로운 기사를 읽었어요.
I read an interesting article in today's newspaper.
신문에서 = 'in the newspaper'; 흥미롭다 = 'interesting'.
그 사건에 대한 기사가 모든 신문에 났어요.
An article about that incident came out in every newspaper.
~에 대한 기사 = 'an article about ~'; 기사가 나다 = 'an article comes out'.
요즘은 종이 신문보다 온라인 기사를 더 많이 봐요.
These days I read online articles more than paper newspapers.
온라인 기사 = 'online article'; ~보다 더 많이 = 'more than ~'.
nuance: 기사 means a news article or report — a single written piece of journalism, whether in a newspaper, magazine, or online. It is the concrete unit of content, distinct from 언론 (the press as an institution) and 보도 (the act of reporting). Note that 기사 is a homonym: it also means 'driver' (운전기사), so context decides the meaning.
mistakes: Confusing the two senses of 기사 — 'news article' versus 'driver (운전기사)'; rely on context.
Using 기사 for the abstract media institution; that is 언론, while 기사 is one specific article.
